To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neural abstractive models hallucinate, pretrained models are better, and entailment metrics are better correlated with faithfulness.

1. Neural abstractive summarizers are prone to hallucinate information, 2. Human evaluations of factual and faithfulness are necessary to better understand the limitations of these models, 3. Pretrained models are better summarisers, 4. Entailment based metrics correlate well with faith

(1) pretrained models are better than non pretrained models for abstrative document summarization; (2) human evaluations of faithfulness and factuality are necessary to evaluate the quality of summaries; and (3) textual entailment metrics are better correlated with human judgments of factuality than standard metrics
In summary, our research is concerned with
the faithfulness of abstractive summarizers.
the question of faithfulness in abstractive summarisation and the role that pretrained models play in improving faithfulness.
the question of faithfulness in abstractive summarizations and how to evaluate them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state of the art in abstractive summarizations is not faithful, but pretrained models do generate more faithful summaries.
pretrained models are more factual and faithful than the baseline models but still have a significant amount of hallucinations in the generated summaries.
the faithfulness of the model is highly correlated with its factuality and that factuality of the model can be evaluated with the help of entailment metrics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that faithfulness and factuality are important aspects of summarization, and pretrained neural abstractive models have better faithfulness and factfulness than non pretrained neural abstrative models.

we have analyzed the limitations of current abstractive summarizers, identified faithfulness as an important metric for evaluating summarizers and shown that pretrained models are more likely to generate factual and faithful summaries.
pretrained language models are better at generating factual and faithful summaries, but they still hallucinate a substantial amount of content.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the faithfulness of the model generated summaries should be considered in the evaluation of summarization systems, and we believe this is a necessary step towards the evaluation of faithfulness in open ended text generation tasks.
faithfulness is a crucial property that needs to be considered for abstractive summarizers and we hope that this work will lead to further improvements in this direction.
the standard likelihood objective is a poor choice for training abstractive summarizers, and that the faithfulness problem can only be mitigated by using other training and decoding criteria.
